title: Spin-One Secondary Pairing in Two-Flavor Color Superconductivity: Spinful Relativistic Superfluidity and Anomaly Matching
abstract: We study secondary pairing in the two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) phase, where the residual ungapped quarks form a same-chirality $J^P=1^+$ condensate driven by an attractive instanton-induced interaction. We determine its symmetry realization, quasiparticle structure, anomaly matching, and low-energy effective theory. The pairing gap is necessarily nodal; in particular, the complex axial state has two point nodes and realizes a spinful relativistic superfluid. This state preserves the full chiral symmetry ${\rm SU}(2)_{\rm L}\times{\rm SU}(2)_{\rm R}$ while breaking the modified baryon-number symmetry ${\rm U}(1)_{\tilde{\rm B}}$ and spatial rotations, with rotations about the nodal axis locked to the condensate phase. This locking gives rise to a Berry term, the Mermin-Ho relation, and a type-B orientational Nambu-Goldstone mode in addition to the superfluid phonon. We also show how anomaly matching is reorganized by secondary pairing: the perturbative mixed ${\rm SU}(2)_{\rm L,R}^2{\rm U}(1)_{\tilde{\rm B}}$ anomaly is realized by a Wess-Zumino coupling of the superfluid phonon, whereas the ${\rm SU}(2)_{\rm L}$ and ${\rm SU}(2)_{\rm R}$ Witten anomalies are carried by the point-node Bogoliubov-de Gennes flavor doublets. The resulting theory provides a concrete dense-QCD realization of a spinful relativistic superfluid with nodal fermions required by anomaly matching.
summary: This work analyzes secondary pairing in color-superconducting quark matter, establishing a spinful relativistic superfluid state characterized by nodal fermions. The authors use anomaly matching to show how the residual symmetries are preserved or broken, leading to a rich low-energy effective theory containing both superfluid and orientational Nambu-Goldstone modes.
main_problem: The study investigates secondary pairing in the two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) phase of dense QCD, linking this pairing to anomaly matching and the resulting spinful relativistic superfluidity.
main_result: The complex axial pairing state is favored, realizing a spinful relativistic superfluid with point nodes, where anomaly matching is resolved by the superfluid phonon and nodal quasiparticles.
method: The analysis employs symmetry realization studies, anomaly matching techniques using gauge-invariant forms, and Ginzburg-Landau analysis to determine the low-energy effective theory.
model_or_system: The system is two-flavor QCD at high density ($\mu_u = \mu_d = \mu$) in the 2SC phase, considering secondary pairing of residual quarks.
key_observables: Pairing gap ($\Delta$), quasiparticle spectrum $E_\chi(\mathbf{p})$, superfluid phonon ($\phi$), Berry term, and the low-energy effective Lagrangian ($\mathcal{L}_{IR}$).
important_parameters: High baryon density ($\mu$), weak-coupling regime (GL analysis), and the specific axial vs. polar condensate structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the massless limit for residual quarks and relies on weak-coupling approximations for the GL analysis.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the symmetry realization and quasiparticle structure of the secondary pairing, determining the preferred nodal state via GL analysis, and finally constructing the low-energy effective theory by matching anomalies.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of emergent topological terms (Berry phase, Mermin-Ho relation) and the explicit mechanism for anomaly matching in a condensed matter analogue of high-energy physics is highly relevant for understanding exotic superfluid phases.
